name: Last Number
description: You are given a multiset $$$S$$$. Initially, $$$S = \{1,2,3, \ldots, n\}$$$. You will perform the following operation $$$n-1$$$ times. Choose the largest number $$$S_{\text{max}}$$$ in $$$S$$$ and the smallest number $$$S_{\text{min}}$$$ in $$$S$$$. Remove the two numbers from $$$S$$$, and add $$$S_{\text{max}} - S_{\text{min}}$$$ into $$$S$$$. It's easy to show that there will be exactly one number left after $$$n-1$$$ operations. Output that number.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. Their description follows. For each test case, one single line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^9$$$) — the initial size of the multiset $$$S$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output an integer denoting the only number left after $$$n-1$$$ operations.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1810H — Last Number [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
